newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares inched up for the second straight session on Friday and analysts saw another rise on Monday, saying the bourse had a chance to break out of its current sideways trend.
"The strong buying after price fixing of some large-cap, fundamentally sound stocks signals there could be significant demand," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Analysts were surprised by the 9.8-percent fall of one such large-cap stock, paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, whose low turnover and strong post-price fixing buying suggested the scale of the fall may have been accidental.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 13,670.3 points and turnover rose 7.1 percent to 72.7 million zlotys ($25.9) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 48 to 22 with 13 stocks flat.

Analysts said top gainer food trader and producer Agros rose 7.9 percent to 68 zlotys ($24.2) in active trade in speculation on the size and pricing of a planned new issue to be voted on at Friday's extraordinary shareholders meeting.
Managemment has proposed an issue of 3,425,000 new shares.
Continuous trade turnover was at 5.9 million zlotys ($2.1 million) with two stocks down, one up and four flat.
NFI units rose 1.6 percent to 156.5 zlotys ($55.7) in regular bourse trade and fell the same amount to 155.5 zlotys ($55.3 million) in continuous trade.
Combined NFI turnover on the two markets was at 59 million zlotys ($20.1), lower than Thursday's 87 million zlotys ($31 million, which had exceeded share turnover.
